data: Before we head out, how about we each catch 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, and the 50 tons left will double back to 100 for next month. It’s the largest total catch we can keep taking month after month without shrinking the lake. My family taught me to leave enough fish for tomorrow, and I want this lake supporting all our families for years. Let’s agree on that equal share and review everyone’s catches together afterward. John, are you on board?

I’m with you, Luke—I'll keep my catch to 10 tons. My family has depended on this lake for years, and an equal share gives us a steady living without putting the village’s future at risk. Let’s check the reported catches each month and talk through any problems before we fish again. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want the next generation to have that chance too. If the lake ever starts a month below 100 tons, let’s agree on smaller whole-ton shares before fishing so it can recover. Jack, will you join us at 10 tons this month?

I’m in for 10 tons this month. A dependable living for all five families beats a big catch now and an empty lake later. Let’s stick to the equal shares and check the catch reports together afterward. John, you’re the last to weigh in—will you join us?

I’m on board—10 tons for me this month. That gives us all a good income while leaving the lake ready for next month. Let’s meet again when the catch reports are out and make sure we’re keeping our agreement.
Glad we’ve all agreed: 10 tons each this month. Let’s meet back here once the catch reports are out. Here’s to a good month’s fishing—and plenty left for the next one.
